topic: Weather, Seasons, and Climate in Daily Life

headwords.definition: the condition of the air outside at a particular time and place
examples: The weather was warm enough for lunch outside.
Mountain weather can change before hikers have time to return.

headwords.definition: the state of the weather or environment at a certain time
examples: Driving conditions became dangerous when fog covered the highway.
The race will continue only if wind conditions remain safe.

headwords.definition: a measurement of how hot or cold something is
examples: The temperature dropped ten degrees after sunset.
I checked the water temperature before letting the children swim.

headwords.definition: a unit used for measuring temperature
examples: It was only five degrees when I left for work.
Even a two-degree rise can make my bedroom uncomfortable at night.

headwords.definition: pleasantly warm and neither very hot nor very cold
examples: We had a mild winter, so the lake never froze.
The afternoon was mild enough for my grandmother to sit in the garden.

headwords.definition: comfortable and enjoyable
examples: A light breeze made the walk surprisingly pleasant.
The temperature is pleasant now, but it will become hotter by noon.

headwords.definition: likely to become different several times in a short period
examples: Spring weather is changeable here; sunshine can turn to rain within an hour.
I packed both a sweater and sunglasses because the forecast looked changeable.

headwords.definition: staying calm and unlikely to change soon
examples: The weather should remain settled throughout the holiday weekend.
Farmers used the settled spell to finish work that rain had delayed.

headwords.definition: one of the main periods of the year with its own typical weather
examples: Autumn is my favorite season because the air becomes cooler and clearer.
The rainy season usually begins in late May.

headwords.definition: the season after winter when plants begin growing again
examples: In spring, I start walking to work again as the days become longer.
The park fills with flowers during the first weeks of spring.

headwords.definition: the warmest season of the year
examples: We eat dinner on the balcony during summer.
Last summer was so dry that the city restricted garden watering.

headwords.definition: the season between summer and winter when many leaves fall
examples: The trees outside my window turn orange in autumn.
Cool autumn evenings are perfect for long walks.

headwords.definition: the coldest season of the year
examples: Our heating bill rises sharply every winter.
I visit my parents more often in winter because we enjoy quiet evenings indoors.

headwords.definition: a regular difference that happens as one season becomes another
examples: The first cold nights are a clear sign of seasonal change.
Seasonal change affects when local farmers plant and harvest crops.

headwords.definition: the process of changing from one season or condition to another
examples: The transition from winter to spring is slow in mountain towns.
I adjust my sleep schedule during the transition to shorter days.

headwords.definition: hot weather or a high temperature
examples: The midday heat forced us to shorten our walk.
I opened every window once the evening heat began to fade.

headwords.definition: light and warmth that come directly from the sun
examples: After a week of rain, the sunshine brought everyone back to the park.
This room gets plenty of sunshine in the morning.

headwords.definition: an unusually long period of very hot weather
examples: During last July's heatwave, the library stayed open as a public cooling space.
The heatwave lasted six days and made it difficult to sleep at night.

headwords.definition: containing a lot of water in the air and feeling uncomfortable
examples: The air was so humid that my clothes felt damp after a short walk.
I find humid evenings more tiring than dry heat.

headwords.definition: the amount of water in the air
examples: High humidity made the thirty-degree temperature feel much hotter.
The museum controls humidity to protect old paintings.

headwords.definition: having little rain or moisture
examples: The ground remained dry because the shower lasted only a few minutes.
My skin becomes dry when indoor heating runs all day.

headwords.definition: a long period with too little rain
examples: The drought left the reservoir at its lowest level in years.
Farmers changed crops after several seasons of drought.

headwords.definition: a cooler area protected from direct sunlight
examples: We moved the picnic table into the shade of a large tree.
There was no shade at the bus stop, so passengers stood beside a nearby building.

headwords.definition: weather with a low temperature
examples: The cold made my hands ache while I waited for the bus.
Some plants cannot survive the winter cold without protection.

headwords.definition: uncomfortably cool but not extremely cold
examples: The morning was chilly, so I wore a light jacket.
It became chilly beside the lake as soon as the sun went down.

headwords.definition: extremely cold or at a temperature where water becomes ice
examples: The apartment was freezing when the heating stopped working.
We avoided the trail because freezing rain had covered it with ice.

headwords.definition: a thin layer of ice that forms on cold surfaces
examples: A thin layer of frost covered the car windows at dawn.
Gardeners protected the young plants from overnight frost.

headwords.definition: covered with ice or dangerously slippery
examples: The steps were icy, so I held the railing and walked slowly.
An icy wind made the playground feel colder than the thermometer suggested.

headwords.definition: the amount or period of snow that falls
examples: Overnight snowfall closed several mountain roads.
The city received very little snowfall this winter.

headwords.definition: a severe snowstorm with strong winds
examples: The blizzard reduced visibility so much that drivers could not see the road.
We stayed inside until the blizzard warning ended.

headwords.definition: very light rain made of small drops
examples: A light drizzle began while I was walking home.
The drizzle was not heavy enough to cancel the outdoor market.

headwords.definition: a short period of rain
examples: A brief shower cooled the streets after a hot afternoon.
We waited in a café until the rain shower passed.

headwords.definition: a sudden period of very heavy rain
examples: We were soaked after getting caught in a sudden downpour.
The downpour flooded the entrance to the underground station.

headwords.definition: the amount of rain that falls in a place and period
examples: This region receives most of its rainfall in winter.
Low rainfall has reduced the amount of water available to farms.

headwords.definition: covered with cloud and without direct sunshine
examples: The sky remained overcast, but it never actually rained.
It was an overcast morning with soft light and no shadows.

headwords.definition: having many clouds in the sky
examples: The afternoon will be cloudy with a few sunny breaks.
Cloudy weather kept the beach quiet even though it was warm.

headwords.definition: a light and pleasant wind
examples: A cool breeze came through the open window.
The sea breeze made the hot afternoon comfortable.

headwords.definition: a sudden short burst of strong wind
examples: A strong gust blew my umbrella inside out.
Sudden gusts made it unsafe to continue the boat trip.

headwords.definition: having a lot of wind
examples: It was too windy to eat comfortably outside.
We chose a sheltered path because the coast was especially windy.

headwords.definition: a statement predicting future weather
examples: The forecast says the rain will stop before noon.
I check the weekend forecast before planning a hike.

headwords.definition: to predict what the weather will be like
examples: Meteorologists forecast heavy snow for the northern mountains.
The app forecast a sunny morning, but clouds arrived early.

headwords.definition: a statement about what is expected to happen
examples: The prediction of strong wind led organizers to cancel the concert.
Yesterday's rain prediction turned out to be wrong.

headwords.definition: correct and free from mistakes
examples: The hourly forecast was accurate enough for us to time our walk.
Weather predictions become less accurate several days into the future.

headwords.definition: changing in a way that is difficult to know in advance
examples: Mountain storms are unpredictable, even in summer.
The weather was too unpredictable for an outdoor wedding without a backup venue.

headwords.definition: to look for the latest information
examples: I check the chance of rain before cycling to class.
Please check the road warnings before starting the trip.

headwords.definition: to arrange an activity for a later time
examples: We postponed the match because lightning was moving toward the field.
The school may postpone its picnic until the ground dries.

headwords.definition: the way a person feels at a particular time
examples: Bright morning light often improves my mood.
Rain does not ruin my mood if I already have an indoor plan.

headwords.definition: feeling active and ready to do things
examples: I feel energized after walking outside on a cool morning.
The first sunny day of spring made everyone seem more energized.

headwords.definition: moving or thinking more slowly than usual
examples: Hot, humid afternoons make me feel sluggish at work.
I was sluggish the next morning because the heat had disturbed my sleep.

headwords.definition: feeling less tired and more comfortable
examples: The cooler air after the storm left me feeling refreshed.
I felt refreshed after taking a short walk in the morning sunshine.

headwords.definition: becoming annoyed more easily than usual
examples: I become irritable when a hot bedroom keeps me awake.
The children grew irritable after spending too long in the heat.

headwords.definition: physical reactions to pollen at certain times of year
examples: My seasonal allergies become worse when trees release pollen in spring.
Seasonal allergies sometimes keep me indoors on otherwise beautiful days.

headwords.definition: fine powder from plants that can cause allergies
examples: The weather report warned that pollen levels would be high.
Rain temporarily washed pollen out of the air.

headwords.definition: red and painful skin caused by too much sunlight
examples: I got a painful sunburn after forgetting to reapply sunscreen.
A hat protected my face from sunburn during the long hike.

headwords.definition: unusually severe or dangerous weather
examples: The city opened emergency shelters during the extreme weather.
Extreme weather can interrupt electricity, transport, and medical services at the same time.

headwords.definition: a large amount of water covering normally dry land
examples: The flood damaged shops along the river.
Residents moved upstairs as flood water entered the ground floor.

headwords.definition: to cover a place with too much water
examples: Heavy rain can flood this road within twenty minutes.
A broken drainage pipe flooded the school basement.

headwords.definition: a large uncontrolled fire spreading through natural land
examples: Smoke from the wildfire reached towns many kilometers away.
Firefighters contained the wildfire before it reached nearby homes.

headwords.definition: a powerful tropical storm with very strong winds
examples: The hurricane damaged roofs and knocked down power lines.
Families left the coastal area before the hurricane arrived.

headwords.definition: a violently rotating column of air reaching the ground
examples: The tornado destroyed several buildings along a narrow path.
Sirens warned residents to take shelter from the approaching tornado.

headwords.definition: to leave a dangerous place for safety
examples: Officials told the neighborhood to evacuate before the river rose further.
Hospital staff practiced how to evacuate patients during a fire.

headwords.definition: a safe place that protects people from danger or weather
examples: The community center served as a shelter during the storm.
Hikers found shelter in a cabin when lightning began.

phrases.text: prepare for a possible power outage
phrases.reusable_core: prepare for a possible power outage

headwords.definition: long-term changes in global or regional climate patterns
examples: Climate change is increasing the frequency of very hot days in some regions.
The city created a long-term climate change plan for water and transport.

headwords.definition: the long-term rise in Earth's average temperature
examples: Global warming raises average temperatures over decades, not just during one summer.
Scientists track ocean temperatures to understand global warming.

headwords.definition: gas or pollution released into the air
examples: The new buses produce fewer emissions than the older diesel vehicles.
Heating buildings is a major source of carbon emissions in cold cities.

headwords.definition: the amount of greenhouse gas caused by a person or activity
examples: Taking the train instead of flying reduced the trip's carbon footprint.
The school measured its carbon footprint before replacing old heating equipment.

headwords.definition: power from sources that naturally replace themselves
examples: The town uses renewable energy from nearby wind turbines.
Solar panels provide renewable energy for the sports center.

headwords.definition: to change in order to manage new conditions
examples: Farmers may need to adapt to longer dry periods.
Cities are adapting streets and parks to cope with hotter summers.

headwords.definition: able to recover from difficulty or damaging events
examples: A resilient power system can recover quickly after a storm.
The community became more resilient by improving drainage and emergency plans.

headwords.definition: to use water, energy, or resources carefully
examples: Residents were asked to conserve water during the drought.
We conserve energy by lowering the heating when nobody is home.
